Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:46: And concerning the punishment for one who comes upon a maidservant, it says in Vayikra Rabbah (parashah 9:5) - these are its words: another explanation, "if he offers it for thanksgiving" (Leviticus 7:12) - this is what Scripture says (Proverbs 14:9), "fools mock at guilt" - Rabbi Yudan said, this fool translates his guilt with his own mouth and says, I am not liable for a sin-offering, nor am I liable for a guilt-offering. Rabbi Yudan in the name of Rabbi Levi said, these are people who treat relations with maidservants as permitted in this world - the Holy One, blessed be He, hangs them by the crown of their heads in the future to come: (Psalms 68:22), "but God shall strike the head of His enemies, the hairy crown of one who walks in his guilt" - all the people shall say, that man's guilt shall consume him - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:47: Further, they said in Tractate Derech Eretz Rabbah, found among us in manuscript, and copied in the Yalkut (Parashat Ki Tetzei, siman 931): one who comes upon a maidservant is liable for fourteen prohibitions and karet [excision] by Heaven: for "you shall not sow your vineyard with mixed seed," for "you shall not plow [with an ox and donkey together]," for "you shall not wear sha'atnez," for "you shall not murder," for "you shall not commit adultery," for "you shall not steal," for "you shall not covet," and "you shall not testify falsely," and for [relations with] a father's wife, and for a brother's wife, for a maidservant, for a harlot, for a menstruant, for a foreign woman. If he was an Israelite and profaned himself and his seed with a Gentile woman, he shall have none who is "awake" among the wise nor "answers" among the students; and if he was a priest, he shall have no son to bring an offering to the LORD of Hosts - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:48: Further, they said in Sanhedrin (82a), on the verse (Malachi 2:11), "Judah has betrayed, and an abomination has been done in Israel" - Rav said, "Judah has betrayed" - this is idolatry, and so it says (Jeremiah 3:20), "you have betrayed Me, house of Israel, says the LORD"; "and an abomination has been done in Israel" - this is homosexual relations, and so it says (Leviticus 18:22), "and you shall not lie with a male as one lies with a woman; it is an abomination"; "for Judah has profaned the holiness of the LORD which He loves" - this is a harlot [kedeshah], and so it says (Deuteronomy 23:18), "there shall be no kedeshah among the daughters of Israel"; "and has married the daughter of a foreign god" - this refers to one who comes upon a Gentile woman. And it is written after it, "the LORD shall cut off, for the man who does this, one who is awake and one who answers" - if he is a Torah scholar, he shall have none who is "awake" among the wise nor "answers" among the students; and if he is a priest, he shall have no son to bring an offering to the LORD of Hosts. Rabbi Chiya bar Avuya said, whoever comes upon a Gentile woman is as though he intermarried with idolatry, as it is said, "and has married the daughter of a foreign god" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:49: Further, in the Midrash (on Proverbs 5:3), "for the lips of a strange woman drip honey" - my son, beware of a harlot, lest she deceive you with the words of her lips, and lest she lead you astray after her voice. Why? "But her end is bitter as wormwood, sharp as a two-edged sword" - He said to him, my son, just as a sword devours from both its sides, so she destroys a person's life, both from the life of this world and from the life of the World to Come. What is written after it? "Her feet go down to death" - that she brings a person down to the depths of death, and this is harsh afflictions. "Her steps take hold of Sheol" - although he is punished with afflictions in this world, he is not saved from the judgment of Gehinnom - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:50: And concerning the punishment for one who comes upon a married woman, and upon an unmarried woman without the seven wedding blessings, it is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Tazria, page 44b) - these are its words: from here we learn, a bridegroom and bride, once they are blessed with the seven blessings, become bound as one, in the pattern of what is above - and therefore whoever comes to unite with another woman, behold he blemishes the union, as it were creating two domains above, since the union of Knesset Yisrael is with the Holy One, blessed be He, alone, whether at a time He is in mercy or at a time He is in judgment.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:51: Come and see, whoever unites with another woman is as though he acts falsely against the Holy One, blessed be He, and against Knesset Yisrael - and therefore the Holy One, blessed be He, does not give him repentance [in the ordinary way]; it depends on repentance until he departs from the world - this is what is written (Isaiah 22:14), "surely this iniquity shall not be atoned for you until you die" - and when? At the hour he enters repentance into that world, and must receive his punishment.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:52: Rabbi Elazar said, this one who acts falsely against Knesset Yisrael shall not be accepted in repentance until he is judged in the judgment of Gehinnom - all the more so one who acts falsely against Knesset Yisrael and against the Holy One, blessed be He - and all the more so if he burdens the Holy One, blessed be He, to create the image of a mamzer in another woman, weakening the retinue of the King.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:53: Rabbi Chiya opened and said, "whoever robs his father and his mother" (Proverbs 28:24) - "his father" is the Holy One, blessed be He, and "his mother" is Knesset Yisrael. What is "robs"? As it is said (Isaiah 3:14), "the plunder of the poor is in your houses" - and who is this? Whoever desires another woman who is not his true match. We have learned there: whoever enjoys this world without a blessing is as though he robs the Holy One, blessed be He, and Knesset Yisrael, as it is written, "whoever robs his father and his mother." "Whoever enjoys this world" - a general term - this is one who cleaves to a woman to enjoy from her, and even though she is unmarried, and he enjoyed from her without a blessing, it is as though he robs the Holy One, blessed be He, and Knesset Yisrael. Why? Because their [the bride and groom's] union is with the seven blessings. And if this is so for an unmarried woman, one who cleaves to another woman who stands in the pattern of what is above, in a union of the seven blessings - all the more so. "He is a companion to a destroyer" - this is Jeroboam, as they have established. "And says, there is no transgression" - for he says, behold, she is unmarried, why is this forbidden? Because of this, "he robs his father and his mother," and moreover, "he is a companion to a destroyer" - who is "a destroyer"? One who blemishes the pattern and repair of what is above - all the more so one who desires his fellow's wife, to cleave to her, who blemishes more - and therefore he is forever blemished: "a destroyer" - who blemishes above, blemishes below, and blemishes his own soul - this is what is written, "a destroyer," and it is written (Proverbs 6:32), "he destroys his own soul who does it."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:54: And concerning the punishment for one who comes upon a Gentile woman, it is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Chayei Sarah, page 131): whoever cleaves to a woman of the other nations who worship idols becomes impure, and that child born to him receives upon himself a spirit of impurity. And if you say, but this comes from the side of his father, why should he receive upon himself a spirit of impurity? Come and see, for first his father became impure at the time he cleaved to that woman who is impure, and since he sinned and became impure with that woman who is impure, all the more so his child born from her shall receive a spirit of impurity - and moreover, he transgressed the Torah, as it is written (Exodus 34:14), "for you shall not bow to another god, for the LORD, jealous is His Name" - because He is jealous over this covenant. And it said further, come and see, this one who brings the holy covenant into that woman of the other nations causes himself to become impure, and causes another place to become impure - and therefore it is written (Proverbs 30:21), "under three things the earth trembles" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:55: Further, in the Zohar (Parashat Va'etchanan, page 266a), while they were walking, Rabbi Abba said, what is the meaning of (Jeremiah 2:13), "Me they have forsaken, the fountain of living waters, to hew for themselves cisterns, broken cisterns," and so on? "Me they have forsaken" - this is whoever acts falsely with the holy sign - and in what does he act falsely with it? That he brings it into another domain, called "broken cisterns" - for the nations of the world, worshippers of idols, are called "broken cisterns," and Israel's is called a well of clear waters that go out and flow from it, as it is said (Song of Songs 4:15), "and flowing streams from Lebanon," and "flowing streams from within your well" (Proverbs 5:15), and it is written (Song of Songs 4:15), "a garden fountain, a well of living waters." "Which cannot contain the water" - what is this? Rather, that river which flows and goes out waters the whole garden and saturates every single place, as we have established, until it fills that place, the garden called "a well of living waters," and from there the upper and lower beings are nourished, along the lines of (Genesis 2:10), "and from there it divides" - and all those sides on the side of the left are not watered from that spring of flowing waters, since they are from the side of the other nations - and whoever acts falsely with the holy Name attaches, on that side, to "broken cisterns, which cannot contain the water," and did not enter there. And whoever merits to guard it merits to be watered from that flowing stream, in this world and in the World to Come - this is what is written (Jeremiah 31:12), "and you shall be like a watered garden, like a spring whose waters do not fail" - and he merits that that supernal well is filled to flow blessings above and below. Woe to whoever acts falsely with the holy Name, for he thereby acts falsely with the supernal Name, and moreover causes this well to not be blessed - of him we read (Deuteronomy 22:19), "for he has brought forth an evil name upon a virgin of Israel" - "a virgin of Israel" precisely - to this point, relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:56: And concerning the punishment for one who comes upon a menstruant, maidservant, foreign woman, or harlot, it says in the Tikkunim (page 59b) - these are its words: and all the adhesions of the poison of death are her feet, and of them it is said (Proverbs 5:5), "her feet go down to death" - and they are the eighteen adhesions [corresponding] to those who pray the eighteen blessings of the prayers, and of them it is written (Genesis 8:21), "and I shall no longer strike every living thing as I have done" - for those who pray the eighteen blessings. And whoever causes the waters of the Flood to grow strong is one who spills the waters of the seed of the covenant of circumcision into a menstruant, maidservant, Gentile woman, or harlot - and a torn animal [treifah] never lives, for wherever [impurity] attaches to a person through his sins, it kills - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:57: Further, in the Tikkunim (page 78b): three husks of the foreskin there are: "destroyer" [mashchit], "anger" [af], and "wrath" [cheimah], corresponding to the sin of the foreskin - as they established in the prayer, "and He, being merciful, shall atone for iniquity, and shall not destroy" - this is "destroyer"; "and shall increase turning away His anger" - this is "anger"; "and shall not stir up all His wrath" - this is "wrath." And whoever brings the sign of the covenant into a foreign domain, these four rule over him - this is what is written (Genesis 7:19), "and the waters prevailed very, very greatly upon the earth" - "upon the earth" being his own body - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:58: Further, in the Tikkunim (page 85a): this sin mentioned truly resembles blemishing the Sabbath and carrying out from a private domain into a public domain - these are its words: whoever uproots an object from its place and places it outside its place is as though he uprooted the Tree of Life, which is the covenant, and places it in a foreign domain - whoever does this causes his own soul to be uprooted from its own domain and placed in another domain, which is the gallbladder and the spleen [bitterness] - and this caused Israel to be uprooted from the land of Israel and exiled to a foreign land, which is a public domain - and so it is with whoever brings his own holy sign of the covenant into a foreign domain - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:59: Further, in the Tikkunim (there, page 97b): in this manner, whoever goes out from a private domain and goes into a public domain, or emits seed from the holy sign of the covenant and brings it into a foreign domain, it is as though he planted the tree of good and evil - and therefore this person who plants into a menstruant, maidservant, Gentile woman, or harlot, of him it is said (Exodus 20:4), "you shall not make for yourself a carved image or any likeness" - and concerning the daughter [child] made in this manner, she is called a "molten image" [masekhah] - and of them it is said (Deuteronomy 27:15), "cursed is the man who makes a carved or molten image," and so on, "and places it in secret" - what is "in secret"? In the secret of the world - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:60: Further, concerning the punishment for one who comes upon a Gentile woman and upon a menstruant, in the Zohar (Parashat Shemot, page 3a) - these are its words: there are three that push the Shechinah from the world, and cause the dwelling of the Holy One, blessed be He, not to be in the world, and people cry out and their voice is not heard, and these are they: whoever has relations with a menstruant - because there is no impurity as strong in the world as the impurity of the menstruant; the impurity of the menstruant is harsher than all the impurity in the world - he becomes impure, and everyone who touches him becomes impure with him; wherever they go, the Shechinah is pushed away before them. And moreover, he causes evil illnesses upon himself and upon that offspring he begets, for once a person approaches that impurity that clings to him, and he becomes impure in all his own limbs, the offspring he begets at that hour draws upon himself a spirit of impurity, and shall be in impurity all his days - for the very structure and foundation of his being is a great and powerful impurity, more than any impurity in the world - for the moment a person approaches a menstruant, that impurity clings to him, as it is written (Leviticus 15:24), "and her impurity shall be upon him."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:61: And whoever has relations with "the daughter of a foreign god," who brings the holy covenant, the sign of the covenant, into another domain, of whom it is written (Malachi 2:11), "and has married the daughter of a foreign god" - and we have learned, there is no jealousy before the Holy One, blessed be He, except the jealousy of the holy covenant, which is the sign of the holy Name and the secret of faith. What is written? (Numbers 25:1), "and the people began to fornicate with the daughters of Moab" - immediately, "and the anger of the LORD was kindled against Israel." The heads of the people, who knew and did not protest, were punished first, as it is written (ibid. 25:4), "take all the heads of the people and hang them before the LORD, against the sun." Rabbi Abba said, what is "against the sun"? Against the covenant, which is called "sun" - and of them it is said (Psalms 84:12), "for a sun and a shield is the LORD God" - "sun and shield," this is the holy covenant: just as the sun shines and illuminates the world, so the holy covenant shines and illuminates a person's body. "A shield" - just as a shield protects a person, so the holy covenant shields a person. And whoever guards it, no harm in the world can approach him - and this is "against the sun." The heads of the people shall be seized in every single generation for this sin, if they know [and do not protest], for this sin is upon them - to arouse the Holy One, blessed be He's jealousy for this covenant.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:62: Whoever brings this holiness into another domain - of him it is written (Exodus 20:3), "you shall have no other gods before Me; you shall not bow to them nor serve them, for I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God" - and it is all one jealousy, and therefore the Shechinah is pushed away from before him.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:63: Whoever acts falsely against the holy covenant sealed in a person's flesh is as though he acts falsely against the holy Name, blessed be He - whoever acts falsely against the seal of the King acts falsely against the King himself - he has no portion in the God of Israel unless through the power of constant repentance.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:64: Rabbi Yosei opened and said, "and the children of Israel forsook the LORD, and He sold them," and so on - what is "forsook"? That they pushed away from themselves the holy covenant, [i.e.,] they circumcised but did not "uncover" [complete it properly] - until Devorah came and inspired all Israel in this, as it is written (Judges 5:2), "when the leaders lead in Israel, when the people volunteer, bless the LORD."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:65: Whoever kills his own children - such as one whose wife becomes pregnant and he causes her to lose the child in the womb - destroys the building of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His craft. There is one who kills a person, and this one kills his own children. He commits three evils that the whole world cannot bear, and therefore the world dissolves little by little, unnoticed, and the Holy One, blessed be He, departs from the world, and sword, famine, and plague come upon the world - and these are: he kills his own children; he destroys the building of the King; he pushes away the soul that goes and wanders in the world and finds no rest - and therefore the spirit of the Holy One, blessed be He, performs, as it were, weeping, and the world is judged with all these judgments. Woe to that person, woe to him - better for him that he never be created in the world. Happy are Israel, who, even while in the exile of Egypt, guarded themselves from all these three - to this point, relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:66: And concerning what it said (Psalms 45:4), "gird your sword upon your thigh, mighty one" - according to the first explanation, the meaning is that the sword that avenges the covenant is what collects from one who blemishes the covenant - and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explained at length (Zohar, Parashat Va'era, page 26a) - these are its words: Rabbi Shimon opened and said (Job 19:29), "be afraid of the sword, for wrath brings the punishments of the sword, that you may know there is a judgment" - "sadun" [there is a judgment] is written [with an extra letter, hinting at "Shaddai"] - "be afraid of the sword" - which sword? This is the sword that avenges the vengeance of the covenant, for this sword stands ready to watch whoever acts falsely with the covenant - for whoever acts falsely with the covenant, the vengeance taken from him is by this sword, as it is written, "for wrath brings the punishments of the sword" - why? Because whoever acts falsely with the covenant separates desire, and does not guard what should be guarded, and does not give to its [proper] place, since it is not aroused toward its own place.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:67: And whoever guards this covenant causes it to be aroused toward its place, and supernal and lower beings are blessed - who arouses this covenant toward its place? When the righteous are found in the world. From where do we know this? From here (Exodus 6:4), "and I also established My covenant with them, to give them the land of Canaan, the land of their sojournings [megureihem], in which they sojourned [garu]" - what is "their sojournings"? Along the lines of "be afraid [guru] of the sword" - because it is a place in which fear [magor] settles in the world - and therefore, "be afraid of the sword" - "in which they sojourned," from the day they drew near to the Holy One, blessed be He, they placed fear in it, a fear, and a supernal fear, in it, to guard His commandments - for if a person does not cast this fear upon his own head, he shall never fear the Holy One, blessed be He - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:68: Further, concerning the merit of one who guards the sign of the covenant, and the punishment of one who blemishes it, it is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Lech Lecha, page 94a) - these are its words: another verse it opened and said, "had not the LORD been my help, my soul would soon have dwelt in silence [Dumah]" (Psalms 94:17) - we have learned, through what did Israel merit not to descend into Gehinnom and not be handed over into the hand of Dumah [the angel of the grave]? Only through this sign - for we have learned, at the hour a person leaves the world, how many bands of destroying angels are appointed over him; they lift their eyes and see this sign, that it is the sign of holiness, and separate from him, and he is not given into the hand of Dumah below, to Gehinnom - for whoever is handed over into his hand certainly descends to Gehinnom. And from this sign, supernal and lower beings fear, and evil judgments do not rule over a person if he merits to guard this sign, since it is attached to the holy Name of the Holy One, blessed be He. Since King David did not guard this sign of the covenant properly, the kingship was removed from him and he was exiled from Jerusalem - he immediately feared and thought he would be handed over to Dumah and die in that world, until he was told the good news, as it is written (II Samuel 12:13), "the LORD has also removed your sin; you shall not die" - at that hour he opened and said, "had not the LORD been my help, my soul would soon have dwelt in silence" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:69: And the merit of one who guards the covenant is explained. Also his punishment, in that it said that because he did not guard the sign of the covenant properly he thought he would be handed over to Dumah - had the Holy One, blessed be He, not been his guardian and advocate, as explained in the Zohar (Parashat Bereishit, page 8b) - and if David feared Dumah, even though the matter was permitted, for whoever went out to the wars of the house of David would write his wife a bill of divorce [as a precaution] (see Shabbat 56a) - and nevertheless, since he did not guard the sign of the covenant properly, his Torah did not suffice to protect him from suffering - and our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Sanhedrin 93b) that King David, peace be upon him, was head of the Sanhedrin, and the law followed him everywhere, as it is said (I Samuel 16:18), "and skilled in speech," that the law followed him everywhere - one who blemished it without hesitation, who shall be his advocate? Shall he not certainly be handed over into the hand of Dumah?
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:70: And behold, nevertheless we find that David accepted mortification and suffering through fasting, as it is said (Psalms 109:24), "my knees are weak from fasting" - and did not his being exiled from his kingdom appear to be because of what he sinned with Uriah, whom he killed by the sword of the children of Ammon? He said there, in Parashat Bereishit, that concerning what he sinned with Uriah, punishment was written against him and he accepted it - and "punishment was written" means what the prophet Nathan told him (II Samuel 12:11), "behold, I raise up evil against you from your own house" - one who has sinned in the covenant, how much must he grieve with mortification and fasting all his days, as David did.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:71: And if one should say, whoever says that Torah atones for sin - was not King David, peace be upon him, occupied with Torah more than we are occupied, as they, of blessed memory, explained, and had the Holy Spirit within him - why did he mortify himself in vain, and not rely on his occupation with Torah day and night to atone for his sin? Rather, certainly what they said, that Torah atones, is along the lines of what the pious Rabbeinu Yonah, peace be upon him, explained in Sha'arei Teshuvah (Gate 1, letter 47), concerning what our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Rosh Hashanah 18a), that one occupied with acts of kindness has his sins atoned - that its explanation is that they suspend suffering from him until he repents; so too one occupied with Torah - the atonement is that suffering is prolonged for him until he repents. But certainly he must purify himself from his sins through mortifications and fastings, so that his Torah be desirable, as we elaborated in the Gate of Repentance (chapter 3). And especially one who sinned in the covenant, whose blemish is equal to the whole Torah entirely, for from the merits our Rabbis, of blessed memory, stated concerning it, we know the greatness of the punishment for one who blemishes it, and they elaborated at length on its merit.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:72: In the Tikkunim (page 65) it also explained, concerning the merit of one who guards the covenant, that of him it is said (Deuteronomy 28:10), "and all the peoples of the earth shall see that the Name of the LORD is called upon you" - for YHVH is inscribed in the covenant, as it says (Deuteronomy 30:12), "who shall go up for us to heaven" - the acrostic is MILAH [circumcision], and the final letters are YHVH - and all accusers fear him. And it says further, at the end of page 64: and therefore, whoever guards the covenant of circumcision, which is his seal, death departs from him - which is Satan, the evil inclination, impurity, the hidden one [Tzafoni], the Angel of Death - and it shall not come near him, and he shall not die through it.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:73: And whoever acts falsely with the covenant of circumcision acts falsely with the seal of the King, upon which Shaddai is inscribed on the outside, YHVH within. From where do we know this? From this verse it is implied, (Deuteronomy 30:12), "who shall go up for us to heaven" - the acrostic is MILAH, the final letters YHVH - and certainly, whoever acts falsely with the covenant of circumcision, YHVH and Shaddai depart from him, and Satan rests upon him, who is "another god," a serpent resting in the place of YHVH within, and the poison of death resting in the place of Shaddai without - and this is what the verse says (Numbers 19:20), "he has defiled the sanctuary of the LORD" - if he does not return in repentance and endure much suffering, to remove that serpent from there, and its poison of death, which is a malignant leprosy, through various illnesses and afflictions, until no flesh remains in him, which is dust - and the secret of the matter (Leviticus 14:42), "and he shall take other dust and plaster the house" - because "the serpent's food is dust" (Isaiah 65:25), until it is sustained from that flesh it shall not depart from him. And a poor person is considered as dead: just as death's face changes, so a poor person's face changes - and they have established (Berachot 6b), "vileness is exalted among the sons of men" (Psalms 12:9) - what is "exalted vileness"? Rather, whoever needs [charity from] creatures, his face changes like a chameleon [karum] - and how many bites of suffering that serpent bites him! And moreover, a poor person is considered as a leper: just as a leper, "his head shall be unkempt," and so on (Leviticus 13:45), so a poor person; just as a leper's dwelling is outside the camp (ibid. 13:46), so a poor person is naked and barefoot - and for Israel, poverty is in the place of leprosy.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:74: And it said further shortly after: and if he returns in repentance, the elixir of life descends upon him, which is the Shechinah, of whom it is said (Isaiah 6:10), "and he shall return and be healed" - from these kinds of illnesses, and heals him from the death of poverty, along the lines of (Ezekiel 18:32), "so turn and live" - for Israel, at the time they are poor, are called dead, and concerning them it is said, "return and live." And there is no poverty like the poverty of Torah, for whoever has no Torah is called dead - what is his remedy for that world? Torah, of which it is said (Proverbs 3:18), "it is a tree of life to those who grasp it," and it is a remedy for all illnesses, along the lines of (ibid. 3:8), "it shall be healing to your navel," and so on - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:75: And from this teaching it is understood that whoever has blemished the covenant must endure harsh suffering, close to death, until that flesh in which the sin is marked is consumed. And especially if he blemished it by emitting seed in vain, which is liable for death (Niddah 13a), he must accept upon himself suffering close to death. And the reason is that the blemish in it is a great, all-inclusive blemish, touching upon the very essence of the Name YHVH, including the positive commandments and the negative commandments: "shem" with "Yud-Hei" is 365 [i.e. the negative commandments], "zachar" [alluding to the male covenant] with "Vav-Hei" is 248 [i.e. the positive commandments] (Tikkunei Zohar, there, page 64a) - and behold, in blemishing the covenant, he blemishes every positive and negative commandment, and needs suffering as though he had transgressed all of them individually.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:76: And my teacher, peace be upon him, elaborated further on this matter, to be precise about the language of the teaching that said, "and the secret of the matter, 'and he shall take other dust and plaster the house'" - and this verse is explained in the Tikkunim (pages 102b-103a) concerning the matter of reincarnation. Now, concerning the acceptance of suffering for repentance, it resembles the reincarnated one: just as the reincarnated one needs another building, since the first body was a dwelling for the external force and needs to be nullified, so in his returning through repentance, he consumes the flesh that grew through the external force, by means of mortifications and fastings.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:77: And Rashbi, peace be upon him, needed to further bring the matter that a poor person is considered as dead, to explain that he shall resemble the reincarnated one in all his aspects - that just as the poor person's face turns green, this is the reason for death, that a dead person's face is green. And "how many bites of suffering bite him" - because both the bones and the flesh are repaired in the reincarnated one, since the external force ruled over both, as explained above, that YHVH and Shaddai departed from him and Samael, who is "another god" and his female, rested in his place - and corresponding to YHVH, which was within, "another god" ruled, and corresponding to Shaddai without, its poison of death ruled in the flesh - and therefore both need repair. Now, through poverty - poverty being great, "how many bites of poverty bite him" - it follows that through this the bones too are broken, as though death ruled over them, and through this everything is repaired. And it said that poverty is like death and like the plague of leprosy, as explained there. It follows that poverty is an atonement for this sin.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:78: Also, it explained at the end of the teaching that Torah is a remedy for all wounds and for all illnesses of the soul, along the lines of "it shall be healing to your navel" - and this is if he repents and does not return to his sin again.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:79: And so it is understood from the whole of his words, that blemishing the covenant causes poverty of money and poverty of Torah - and the reason is that since the secret of the covenant is the secret of the river that flows and goes out, it draws all kinds of flow, whether physical flow for the sustenance of the body or spiritual food for the sustenance of souls - and since he has blemished it, both depart; and since he has returned in repentance, both return - and this is what it said, "and if he returns in repentance, the elixir of life descends upon him, which is the Shechinah," and "healed him" from the poverty of Torah - for since the covenant is repaired, he has an ascent to hold fast to the Tree of Life, which is the middle pillar, the place where Torah springs forth.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:80: And the measure of the language is thus: "and there is no poverty like the poverty of Torah" - meaning, as we have said above, that whoever has blemished the covenant is pursued by poverty until he is considered as dead - there is no poverty like the poverty of Torah, and behold he is considered as dead, even if he is wealthy [materially]. And his remedy is that he return in repentance, that he not return to his sin, and occupy himself with Torah, so that it be a balm for his wound - for by ascending above the place of the blemish, he brings the elixir of life to heal the blemish placed there in the covenant, called "living."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:81: And my teacher, peace be upon him, wrote that the elixir of Torah avails only after repentance, which is the abandonment of the sin, and the acceptance of suffering afterward with love. And the reason is that Torah is an elixir of life to purify the husk that is within, while the suffering purifies the flesh from without - as explained above, that "another god" rests in the place of YHVH within, and the poison of death rests in the place of Shaddai without.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:82: And nevertheless, it appears to my humble opinion, when we are precise about his words, "and it is a remedy for all illnesses," as it is said, "it shall be healing to your navel" - that the intent is that Torah is a remedy both for what is without, namely the flesh, and for what is within, namely the bones - and this is "healing to your navel," which is the flesh, and "moisture to your bones," meaning the word "and so on" [in the verse], to be precise about the end of the verse, which is needed for his intent. And the reason is that Torah is like a bandage for a wound: after the bad flesh is consumed, they place a poultice and a bandage to grow good flesh - so the suffering purified the husk both within and without, and this poor person remains afflicted and emaciated, and his bones have withered - and therefore he needs the elixir of Torah, which is moisture for the bones, to moisten them, and it is a bandage for the flesh without - and this is "healing to your navel and moisture to your bones." And this resembles what is explained in the Zohar (Parashat Vayakhel, page 211b) concerning (Malachi 3:20), "and the sun of righteousness shall rise for you who fear My Name," and so on, as explained in the Gate of Fear, end of chapter 13.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:83: And so, included in the repentance for this sin is to be careful in guarding the sign of the Sabbath, the sign of tefillin, and the sign of festivals - and so they explained in the Tikkunim (page 95a) - these are their words: the supernal Hei, the lower Hei, the Vav, the middle pillar, bears both of them - the foundation of everything is the Yud, which is the covenant. Whoever uproots and acts falsely with it uproots everything and it falls from him - and this Yud is the foundation stone, from which the world was founded, and of it is said (Psalms 118:22), "the stone the builders rejected," and so on - it is the foundation of everything, upon which everything is built - and whoever sins concerning the sign of the Sabbath, the sign of tefillin, the sign of festivals, and the sign of the covenant of circumcision, it is as though he uproots it from its place and returns the world to chaos and void - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:84: And since we find that Rashbi, peace be upon him, compared the sign of the covenant to the sign of the Sabbath, the sign of tefillin, and the sign of festivals, it appears that the blemish is equal in all of them, and in all of them one must be careful. And it is already known that our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said (Shabbat 118b), whoever observes the Sabbath according to its law is forgiven all his sins, as it is said (Isaiah 56:2), "who keeps the Sabbath from profaning it [mechalelo]" - do not read "mechalelo" but "mochlin lo" [he is forgiven].
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Holiness 17:85: And especially in the observance of the Sabbath day one must be very careful, for it resembles the sign of the covenant in many things, and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, compared them - these are its words (Zohar, Parashat Yitro, beginning of page 92): "remember the Sabbath day to keep it holy" (Exodus 20:8) - this is the secret of the holy covenant, and because through this covenant all the wellsprings of the organs of the body are established, and it is the inclusion of everything - in this manner the Sabbath is the inclusion of the whole Torah, and all the secrets of the Torah depend on it, and the fulfillment of the Sabbath is the fulfillment of the entire Torah - for whoever guards the Sabbath is as though he guards the entire Torah - to this point.
